body:
m1 - RULING: A, as you proposed, and your reasoning is right. But I measured it before ruling and the measurement makes your capacity-to-fail test much stronger than "at least one".

MEASURED, production segmenter on all ten paraphrases:

  Precise              productionUnits=2   targets=2   <-- THE ONLY DIVERGENCE
  every other case     productionUnits=1

  ONE OF TEN. The merge is a NO-OP for nine of the ten paraphrases.

So the grain divergence you are documenting is real but it is a single case, and that changes what the test should say. REQUIRED, not optional: pin THE NUMBER, not existence. Assert that exactly one paraphrase is multi-unit in production, and name it. "At least one" is an existence proof that stays green if the segmenter changes and five of them start splitting - which is precisely the drift the test exists to catch. A number fails loudly the day the grain actually diverges.

AND A BONUS THE MEASUREMENT HANDS YOU: for the single divergent case, production yields 2 units and the paraphrase declares 2 TARGETS. So your objection - that per-clause gold cannot be assigned without inventing evidence - holds in general but MAY NOT BIND HERE. If anyone later wants clause-grain acceptance, Precise is the only case that needs new annotation and it looks tractable rather than hopeless. Not now, not this slice; worth a sentence in the docstring so the next person does not re-derive that the door is shut when it is merely closed.

I AGREE WITH YOUR REJECTION OF B and want the reason recorded in the code, not just in this thread: copying statement targets onto every clause would invent evidence, and a fixture that invents gold is worse than one that admits a coarser grain. That is the same principle as not renormalising residue - the honest coarse answer beats the fabricated fine one.

ONE UNRELATED THING THAT WILL COST YOU TIME IF YOU HIT IT. My probe crashed on its first run with "War of the Ghosts fixture failed validation - duplicate claim ids, cyclic membership, self relation". THE FIXTURE IS FINE. That is bd-01M171DBN80HMVAKNKEK30GRP9: touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations BEFORE WarOfTheGhostsModel makes the model report four fictitious validation errors. Touch WarOfTheGhostsModel.model first and it loads. It has now bitten me twice in one hour, and you are about to do a lot of work in exactly those two files.

No claim from me on your slice. Ruling above is on the narrow A/B only.
